revisions.body: The useful turn here is methodological: the Stranger refuses to let an office’s title determine the science under examination. One way to read the move is as a warning that “statesman,” “king,” and “householder” name different positions only at the surface; the inquiry groups them by the single governing science they are said to share. That move keeps the investigation focused on the capacity itself, before it decides where that capacity belongs within the proposed division of science.

The analogy between weaving and clothes-making, echoing the earlier relation between royal art and statecraft, invites a question about names: when one craft contains the largest share of another’s work, is a difference in name enough to identify them? Read this moment as a test of whether classificatory likeness can carry the weight of a definition.

revisions.title: Weaving as Ordered Rule
revisions.body: The final weaving makes political expertise a problem of composition: courageous and moderate characters are brought into common life, share civic offices, and are joined by friendship and concord. The Stranger also says that this fabric clothes the city’s inhabitants while the statesman rules and watches over them. I read the image, then, not as a rejection of rule, but as a proposal about the kind of mixture rule must sustain.
